cases.name: from-without-to
cases.description: from= and to= are used together or not at all
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: unknown-date-locale
cases.description: A date locale nobody has translated
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" range="2026-01-01..2026-01-31" local="klingon"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: step-not-a-step
cases.description: a step this notation cannot express is refused
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="fortnight"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: step-old-spelled-out-form
cases.description: the earlier prose form is gone: there is one notation, not two
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="15 minute"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: step-mixes-calendar-and-fixed
cases.description: a month plus fifteen days depends on which is applied first, so it is refused rather than guessed
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="1mo15d"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: step-repeats-a-unit
cases.description: a repeated unit is a typo; summing it would hide the typo instead of reporting it
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="1h30m1h"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: step-without-order-sequential
cases.description: nothing walks the range, so step= would be read by nobody
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" range="2026-01-01..2026-12-31" step="1d"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: weekdays-without-order-sequential
cases.description: the same for the filter: with no walk there is nothing to filter
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" range="2026-01-01..2026-12-31" weekdays="mon..fri"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: weekdays-unknown-name
cases.description: a weekday that does not exist is named rather than silently dropped
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" weekdays="mon..frr"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: weekdays-hyphen-is-not-a-range
cases.description: the range operator is .. everywhere in this language, so mon-fri is not a span
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" weekdays="mon-fri"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: weekdays-under-a-weekly-step
cases.description: a whole week always lands on the same weekday, so the filter would match every row or none
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="1w" weekdays="mon"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: weekdays-under-a-fourteen-day-step
cases.description: 14d fixes the weekday exactly as 2w does — the test is the step's LENGTH, not its spelling
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="14d" weekdays="mon"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: weekdays-under-a-calendar-step
cases.description: a calendar step fixes the weekday too
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential" step="1mo" weekdays="mon"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: walked-from-alone-is-accepted
cases.description: from= with no end is an OPEN axis when the range is walked: no diagnostic at all
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="G"><gen type="date" from="2026-01-01" order="sequential"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>x</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: an-env-locale-with-no-date-translations-says-so
cases.description: A locale can be a perfectly good source of NAMES and still ship no month names — Bambara has a name pack and no DATE_LOCALE.json — so refusing it on <env local=> would forbid the name pack for the dates' sake. This warns instead, and only when the format actually reads the locale: format="YYYY-MM-DD" is the same in every language and says nothing. It used to warn for Afrikaans too, wrongly: the pack SHIPPED the translations and the engine never read them. Seventy locales' DATE_LOCALE.json files are loaded now, so the warning is reserved for locales that truly carry none.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s" local="bm"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" value="2026-03-01..2026-03-05" format="LL"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: two-spellings-of-the-same-range
cases.description: value=, the from/to pair and range= are three ways to say one thing, and the generator reads them in that order and stops. Writing two put one in the file and did nothing with the other: value="2020-05-05" from="1990-01-01" to="1990-12-31" produced 1990-05-11.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" value="2020-05-05" from="1990-01-01" to="1990-12-31" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: today-cannot-also-carry-a-range
cases.description: value="today" is a spelling of the range too, so it cannot carry a from/to: the from/to was discarded and every row came out as today.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" value="today" from="1990-01-01" to="1990-12-31" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-reversed-from-to-is-refused-not-swapped
cases.description: The draw took min and max of the two ends, so a reversed pair produced perfectly plausible dates from a range nobody wrote. The date page already states the rule for plus=: write the smaller bound first, and a typo is refused rather than quietly swapped.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" from="2020-01-01" to="2010-01-01" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-reversed-value-range-is-refused-too
cases.description: The same typo written the other way.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" value="2020-01-01..2010-12-31" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>

cases.name: a-range-in-order-is-accepted
cases.description: The line the check must not cross: an ordinary range, and value="birth" with its own age window, stay accepted.
cases.config: <tdc><env count="2" seed="s"><sequence name="D"><gen type="date" from="2010-01-01" to="2020-01-01" format="YYYY-MM-DD"/></sequence></env><block><line><data>${{D}}</data></line></block></tdc>
